description:
## Why

Tier 3 of the PKIX-7nsf corpus plan: real-wild chains from a CT log (Cloudflare Nimbus, Let's Encrypt Oak). Very high volume, low signal density, but catches divergences curated corpora miss.

## What

Separate sub-project (NOT a blocker for PKIX-7nsf parent — that closes on PKITS + pyca baselines):

1. CT log fetcher: `pkix-difftest/python/fetch-ct.py` (or Rust binary) that hits a CT log's get-entries endpoint and writes chains to a corpus directory.
2. Corpus loader integration: PEM-tree loader (already done in PKIX-7nsf.4) should handle the dumped chains.
3. Baseline run + commit (large output, may need separate storage strategy — e.g., not committed in-tree, just summary).

## Out of scope

- Live monitoring of new CT log entries (that's a service, not a one-shot scrape).
- BC oracle (still deferred per parent bead).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fetcher script + docs.
- [ ] One scraped baseline committed (summary only, raw chains stored externally).
- [ ] Storage-strategy decision documented.

## Filed as

Follow-up to PKIX-7nsf, deferred per the parent bead's 'Recommended decomposition' steps (8).
notes:
Marked blocked 2026-05-10: bead's own description says this is Tier-3 follow-up to PKIX-7nsf, explicitly deferred. Unblock when PKIX-7nsf parent baseline closes and a CT scrape storage strategy is in scope.
Escalated to human 2026-05-11 by do-beads autonomous loop: bead acceptance criterion 'Storage-strategy decision documented' is an open architecture choice (in-tree vs LFS vs external-only with manifest, summary-only commit policy, retention/refresh schedule), not autonomously decidable. The implementation work (fetcher script, loader integration, baseline run) is bounded and clear once that choice is made. Recommendation: pick the storage strategy first, then re-open to a fresh autonomous loop.
Ratified 2026-05-11 (Mark): external-only with manifest.

Storage decisions:
- Scraped corpus lives outside the repo (S3 or equivalent external object store).
- Repo carries a JSON manifest with content hashes (BLAKE3 or SHA-256) + a summary MD of the differential results.
- Refresh cadence: quarterly or on-demand (not automated CI).
- Consistent with how ~/GIT/x509-limbo is handled today (external corpus + in-tree summary).

Rejected: in-tree (repo size), LFS (adds tooling complexity), summary-only-no-manifest (loses reproducibility).

Implementation work: fetcher script (pkix-difftest/python/fetch-ct.py or Rust equivalent), corpus loader integration (already in place per PKIX-7nsf.4 PEM-tree loader), one scraped baseline run with summary committed.

Ready for autonomous claim. Note: this remains parented under PKIX-hbzo (diff-harness completeness) as a Tier-3 follow-up.
title: diff harness: Tier-3 CT log scrape corpus
